# OMP Session Gateway

> Native integration with stock Oh My Pi (OMP) >=18.1.20. No OMP fork, custom build,
> gateway-specific OMP plugin, or publisher credential. v0.7.1 is qualified for stable promotion; publication is pending.
> Keep using OMP in the terminal; the separate gateway discovers collaboration-enabled
> sessions and opens OMP's own encrypted View/Control client in any modern browser, installable as a PWA where the platform supports it. One-time
> setup requires collab.autoStart, Bun 1.4.0, gateway installation, and TUN-mode Tailscale Serve
> with Funnel disabled. No per-session QR scan or link copy. Community project; not affiliated
> with or endorsed by the Oh My Pi maintainers.

## Supported platforms

- Supported and tested in CI on every change (the stock-OMP canaries run daily): Linux, macOS, and Windows gateway hosts; Chrome and Chromium, Edge through Chromium, Firefox, Safari/WebKit, and Android; iPhone and iPad as a WebKit browser, emulated in CI. Supported is not qualified: qualification is the exact hardware matrix below. Lanes: portable-source (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows), browser-core (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, iPhone-class WebKit), browser-notifications (Pixel sizes), windows-service-lifecycle, canary and canary-windows.

## Current qualification boundary

- v0.7.1 is qualified for stable promotion from signed candidate v0.7.1-prealpha.1 (source 861225c9abd9379bf78ac40febb2d99a6d7bbcb3, archive SHA-256 097d457bbeab931304e132d162c9b2fa7860016ac1dc6b88b9f06ac98427d1af) against stock OMP v18.4.2. It hands a tapped notification to the open page instead of reloading it, releases a frozen session list's live-update stream, and has the gateway release event streams that stop reading. Every lane passed on its first attempt in one campaign. No claim for arbitrary builds from main.
- Exact OMP v18.4.2 source: 4620bb8338e0ecace7ea237da9d5088d16068617. Set only collab.autoStart (off/view/control); start participating sessions with plain omp. The gateway reads OMP discovery and queries each host; OMP does not register with the gateway.
- Debian 13 (trixie) x86-64, Linux 6.12.94+deb13-amd64: 83/83 migration/recovery invariants, stock OMP publication/revocation, persistence, tagged-identity denial/exposure, uninstall and resource teardown.
- Mac14,3 / macOS 26.6.1 arm64: doctor 18/18, rollback 23/23, install/rotation/reboot-to-login persistence, real allowlisted identity and forged-header/exposure checks. Positive allowed-user HTTPS was measured on Mac/Pixel, not the tagged Debian CI caller.
- Windows Server 2025 x86-64, build 26100, on a disposable 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM destroyed afterwards: as Administrator, the candidate upgraded published v0.7.0, survived a real reboot and started automatically 71.7 s after interactive logon; doctor 15/18 with only the tagged node's identity, PWA and session checks false; named-pipe publication, View/Control 200, stale generations 409, the Pixel's View and Control, readiness rotation, history-selected rollback and uninstall. Then a standard local account, its token without Administrators or SeSecurityPrivilege, installed the candidate fresh, and after a real reboot the gateway started 30.2 s after that account's logon; doctor 15/18, readiness rotation and uninstall passed as that account. The claim is start at interactive logon, not at boot.
- Pixel 10 Pro / Android 17 build CP3A.260905.009 / Chrome 154.0.8037.57: View read-only, Control writable, prompt accepted, return to directory; same-page recovery: unlock 7,421 ms, Airplane 5,976 ms, Doze 408 ms; all seven forbidden capability sinks detectable and clean.
- Background Web Push on the same Pixel with the installed app closed: Private, Session and Preview delivery on the lock screen in 2.8–3.8 s, one notification each; taps to current Control and View, stale-generation scrub, authoritative clear, permission revocation, lock/resume, Wi-Fi and cellular delivery, Airplane suppression and recovery; ten forbidden sinks clean. Force-stop and Doze outcomes are observed variants, never delivery guarantees.
- Real cloud devices on TestingBot (ADR-032), qualified in the browser: iPhone 17 Pro Max / iOS 26.6 / Safari 26.6, iPad (9th generation) / iPadOS 26.6 / Safari 26.6, and Galaxy S26 (SM-S942B) / Android 16 / Chrome 145.0.7632.159 each passed View read-only, Control writable, prompt accepted and return to directory on the candidate's app bundle, with seven detectable clean capability sinks; TestingBot's test records held no live link, video or screenshots. On the iPhone, the Home Screen app enabled alerts with a real tap, an attention alert arrived in 16.0 s with the app in the background, and its tap opened current Control with a scrubbed address. Limits: Serve saw the workstation's allowlisted login, not a phone's; alerts were proven unlocked with the app in the background, not on the lock screen; lock, Airplane, Doze, force-stop and cellular behavior stay Pixel-only.
- Tailscale Serve over tailnet HTTPS only, TUN mode required, Funnel disabled. Fresh relay check: 1,800 seconds (2026-09-30T00:32:32.439Z–01:02:32.448Z), two transitions, final phase live. The 30-minute check replaces eight hours, as for every mainline release; eight-hour endurance was not rerun or claimed, no historical endurance transfers, and residual prolonged-operation risk is accepted. No bounded-memory-growth claim is made.
- Other Windows versions are supported and CI-tested, including a daily canary that drives stock OMP's named pipe through the gateway, but not qualified. Specialized attention and branch/resume, and new media qualification remain unqualified/unadvertised. Seeded-fixture product media is not release-qualification evidence for these lanes. Android radio changes can still wedge Chrome; the proven same-page recoveries do not remove that limit.
- v0.7.0 is the migration/rollback predecessor. Rolling back restores its notification taps, which reload an open collaboration in the installed Android app, its frozen session list that keeps its live-update stream, and its gateway that can hold a stalled event stream (#321, #327, #328). Gateway rollback does not switch OMP. v0.6.3, further back, embeds OMP 18.3.0's collaboration client; v0.6.2 cannot be installed or run from a standard Windows account (#293, #294); v0.6.0 cannot enable background alerts on iPhone or iPad, because it rejects WebKit's push subscription, which leaves out a null expiration time.
- In v0.5.0 and earlier, the first visit after a gateway upgrade can navigate a pending launch or an open View/Control page back to the directory: the service worker cannot see that a page is in use because Chromium reports each page's creation URL. The first post-release View/Control smoke failures match this navigation. The v0.5.1 fix never navigates from the worker.
- The v0.7.1 published-byte local/Pixel smoke is pending after publication. The v0.7.0 smoke passed on its first attempt across the upgrade from v0.6.3, against Bun's global stock OMP 18.1.20.

## Fork-era release history

- v0.3.0 requires its exact patched OMP v18.1.14 and matching historical instructions. Its qualification does not transfer to the mainline architecture.
